when.quote: Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received.

info.about: The customer's full name or email, used to find their record
info.ask: Could you tell me your full name or the email on your account so I can find your profile?

info.about: Any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, address. They must match the record exactly
info.ask: To verify your identity, please give me two of these: your date of birth, email, phone number or address on file.

info.about: Each credit card account: card type and account open date. The open date decides whether a promo applies
Every credit card transaction: transaction_id, card type, merchant, amount, category, date, rewards_earned
Whether the customer wants all transactions reviewed or only some. Errors in either direction (too many or too few points) count
info.ask: Would you like me to review every transaction on all of your cards, including any that may have been over-credited?

steps.do: Greet the customer. Ask for their name or email and 2 of: DOB, email, phone, address
steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address.

args.customer_name: name the customer gave (or use get_user_information_by_email with the email they gave)

steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address.

steps.do: Confirm that at least 2 of the values given match the record. If they don't, do not share any information
steps.quote: Knowing full name or userID is not enough to verify.

steps.do: Get the current time for the verification log
steps.quote: After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records.
After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records.

steps.do: Fetch all of the user's credit card accounts (card types and open dates)
steps.quote: Recalculate the correct rewards for each transaction based on the card type, transaction category, and any applicable promotions.

steps.do: Fetch all of the user's credit card transactions
steps.quote: Our customer service team has the tools to investigate cash back discrepancies and review your transaction history.

steps.do: Recalculate the correct points for every transaction using the card's rates, merchant exclusions, any promo active at purchase, and floor rounding. Compare with rewards_earned and list every mismatch, whether too high or too low
steps.quote: Ensure your calculation reflects the proper base rate and any active bonus category or promotion at the time of purchase.

steps.do: Tell the customer which transactions are wrong (transaction_id, merchant, points recorded vs. correct points), in both directions. Confirm the transaction_ids with them
steps.quote: Confirm the customer has the correct transaction_id before they submit.

steps.do: Give the customer the cash back dispute tool and explain its arguments (their user_id plus each transaction_id)
steps.if: at least one transaction has a discrepancy
steps.quote: Tool to provide to the user: `submit_cash_back_dispute_0589(user_id: str, transaction_id: str)`

steps.do: Customer submits one dispute for each discrepant transaction
steps.quote: Tell the customer to run the tool with their own user_id and the specific transaction_id for the purchase in question.
Use `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool` to unlock the agent tool `update_transaction_rewards_3847`.

steps.do: Set each disputed transaction's rewards to the independently recalculated value

args.arguments: {transaction_id: the disputed transaction_id, new_rewards_earned: 'X points' (recalculated whole number)}

steps.quote: new_rewards_earned: a string formatted as 'X points' where X is the correct whole-number point value

steps.do: Re-read the transactions to confirm the corrections posted
steps.quote: Confirm the update in credit_card_transaction_history after the tool call completes.

steps.do: Summarize the corrections made (points and dollar value at 1 point = $0.01)
steps.quote: these 'points' should be interpreted as cash back with a conversion rate of 1 point = $0.01

rules.rule: Points earned = floor(amount × rate). Fractions are always truncated
rules.quote: All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number.

rules.rule: Cash back cards store rewards as points: 1 point = $0.01, so points = amount × percent rate × 100
rules.quote: these 'points' should be interpreted as cash back with a conversion rate of 1 point = $0.01

rules.rule: Never use an expected_rewards value from the dispute record. Recompute it independently
rules.quote: Important: Do not rely on any expected_rewards field in the dispute record. Independently verify rates and eligibility.

rules.rule: Diamond Elite Card: 5.0% on all eligible purchases
rules.quote: You earn 5.0% cash back on all eligible purchases posted to your account.

rules.rule: Business Platinum Rewards Card: 4.0% on Travel, Software and Media
rules.quote: Travel, software, and media advertising purchases earn 4.0%.

rules.rule: Business Platinum Rewards Card: 1.5% on all other categories
rules.quote: Purchases outside those categories earn 1.5%.

rules.rule: Business Silver Rewards Card: 10.0% on Travel and Software
rules.quote: Earn 10.0% cash back on eligible travel and software purchases

rules.rule: Business Silver Rewards Card: 1.0% on everything else
rules.quote: Earn 1.0% cash back on all other purchases

rules.rule: Business Silver Rewards Card: these merchants earn only 1.0% whatever their category: Concur, SAP Concur, Expensify, Navan, Apple, Microsoft, Dell, Xbox Game Pass, PlayStation Plus, Nintendo Switch Online, Coursera, Udemy, LinkedIn Learning, Skillshare, Pluralsight
rules.quote: The following specific merchants do NOT earn the 10.0% bonus rate and instead earn the standard 1.0% rate:

rules.rule: Business Silver double cash back: rates ×2 (20% travel/software, 2% other) only if the account was opened between 2024-11-14 and 2025-11-14 and the purchase falls within 6 months of the account open date
rules.quote: New Business Silver Rewards Card customers can earn 2x cash back on all purchases for the first 6 months after opening their account.

rules.rule: The 6-month double cash back window counts from the account open date
rules.quote: The 6-month window begins on your account opening date, not the promotional start date

rules.rule: The account must have been opened within the promo period to get double cash back
rules.quote: You must open your account during the promotional period to qualify

rules.rule: The merchant exclusions still apply during the double promo (an excluded merchant earns 1.0% × 2)
rules.quote: Merchant category exclusions continue to apply (see Exceptions and Exclusions)

rules.rule: EcoCard: 5 points per dollar on Green/Sustainable purchases
rules.quote: Green purchases: Earn $5.00 sustainability points per dollar spent at qualifying green merchants and categories.

rules.rule: EcoCard: 1 point per dollar on everything else
rules.quote: Other purchases: Earn $1.00 sustainability points per dollar.

rules.rule: EcoCard: Target, Walmart, Amazon and ThredUp earn only 1 point per dollar, even on green items
rules.quote: The following specific merchants do NOT earn the higher sustainability points rate ($5.00 points per dollar) and instead earn the standard rate ($1.00 point per dollar):

rules.rule: EcoCard: EV charging earns 5x only at Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint or EVgo. Any other network earns 1x
rules.quote: EV charging only qualifies for green rewards when using one of our 3 certified partner charging networks: Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo.

rules.rule: Green and Sustainable are the same category
rules.quote: Sustainable (same as Green, used interchangeably)

rules.rule: Any category outside a card's bonus categories earns that card's default rate
rules.quote: Purchases in non-bonus categories earn the card’s default rate.

rules.rule: Disputes cover any discrepancy, both over-credited and under-credited transactions
rules.quote: Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received.

jobs.done_when: Every transaction has been recalculated. Each discrepant transaction (too high or too low) has had a dispute submitted by the customer with submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 and its rewards corrected with update_transaction_rewards_3847 to the floor-rounded 'X points' value. The corrections are confirmed in the transaction history and summarized to the customer.

documents.why: Internal procedure for cash back disputes: give the customer submit_cash_back_dispute_0589
Internal procedure for applying resolved dispute corrections with update_transaction_rewards_3847: recalculation rules and the 'X points' format
Rewards are stored as points; 1 point = $0.01; EcoCard is the only true points card
Valid categories; Green = Sustainable; non-bonus categories earn the default rate
Customer-facing statement that agents investigate cash back discrepancies
Business Platinum software qualifying rules and exclusions
Business Silver merchant exclusions from the 10% rate
Business Silver double cash back promo: window and conditions
What counts as green for EcoCard
EcoCard merchant exclusions and EV charging network rule

open_questions: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards__general__004 says to look up resolved disputes in the 'cash_back_disputes database', but no tool for that is named. It is unclear whether disputes submitted with submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 resolve immediately, or whether get_user_dispute_history_7291 (which covers credit card transaction disputes) should be used to check their status before applying corrections.

The documents do not say whether a customer must be told before rewards are reduced on over-credited transactions. The dispute process is framed as covering any 'discrepancy', so this workflow treats over-credits the same as under-credits.

Diamond Elite and Business Platinum have no merchant-level exclusion lists, and no rewards-rate promos were found for them or for EcoCard (the EcoCard promos found are a sign-up bonus and a 0% APR offer, not rate multipliers).
If the user holds other cards, read those cards' own rate documents before recalculating.
